title: Comm-SCI Help
subtitle: Deterministic wrapper guidance: startup, command routing, SCI, quality control, citation

sections.title: Quickstart (Production)
items: Load a ruleset via the folder icon and verify Comm State before first content task.
Connect provider/model in panel, then run Comm Start as standalone command.
Select profile explicitly (for example Profile Expert) and only then ask your task.
Use Comm Anchor and Comm Audit periodically in long sessions.

sections.title: Command Discipline
items: Commands are standalone-only: send only the command token line, no mixed content.
Comm State / Comm Config / Comm Help / Comm Audit are local deterministic renderers.
Comm Stop disables Comm governance flow for following content answers.
Profile switches are explicit and auditable via command history.

sections.title: SCI Workflow
items: After SCI on, select a variant A-H in the next prompt while selection is pending.
SCI Trace steps depend on selected variant and are validated by output contracts.
Use SCI recurse only when SCI is active and you need one-turn deeper analysis.
Use SCI off to return to non-trace content mode.

sections.title: Quality and Language Policy
items: QC-Matrix and Self-Debunking are enforced by contracts for content answers.
QC override values change effective QC targets and are visible in Comm State.
Language policy production keeps user-facing output strict and concise.
Language policy benchmark is for controlled evaluation and regression comparison.

sections.title: Wrapper Components and Effect
items: Provider/Model selection controls runtime behavior and rendering characteristics.
Comm commands change explicit state (profile, SCI mode, overlays, color, policy).
Audit and logs provide traceability for troubleshooting and regression analysis.
Manual test scenarios validate deterministic contracts before release.

sections.title: API keys: plaintext vs encrypted
items: Panel path: Provider & LLM -> API-Key; enter, update, or delete keys per provider.
api_key_plain means local plaintext storage without passphrase prompts.
api_key_enc means local encrypted storage with passphrase prompts.
Passphrase is requested on startup or provider switch only when the target provider uses encrypted key storage.

sections.title: Troubleshooting
items: If a command appears ignored, check standalone formatting and Comm State first.
If panel buttons are clicked rapidly, wait for command completion before next action.
If provider calls fail, validate API key, provider selection and model availability.
If structure drifts, run Comm Anchor and Comm Audit before continuing.
Input-line history is auto-saved in Logs/History on shutdown and auto-loaded at startup.
